chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Ibrahim, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I was accompanying Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) in the journey between Mecca and Medina. When he arrived at the Sanctuary (Haram), he dismounted, performed ritual bath (ghusl), and took his sandals in his hands, then entered the Sanctuary barefoot. So I did what he did. He said: 'O Aban! Whoever does what you saw me do, out of humility for Allah, Allah will erase one hundred thousand bad deeds from him, record for him one hundred thousand good deeds, build for him one hundred thousand levels (of reward), and fulfill for him one hundred thousand needs.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for entering the Haram barefoot out of humility?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s deliberate act of removing his shoes by hand to enter the Haram barefoot, a physical manifestation of tawad‘ (humility) that distinguishes the sacred space. Scholarly tradition interprets the specific reward of 'one hundred thousand' for various spiritual benefits as emphasizing the magnitude of divine grace for such simple, conscious acts of devotion. It serves as a practical guide for pilgrims, linking physical posture in the sanctuary directly to the erasure of sins and the fulfillment of needs.
